identity.description: Higgsfield is an AI image and video generation platform with a web app, a REST API for developers (api.higgsfield.ai), an open-source CLI installed as higgsfield, and an MCP server page for AI agents.
identity.identity_notes: Docs, creator hub, and the higgsfield-ai/cli GitHub repo describe the same generation product. The CLI repo is owned by the higgsfield-ai org. The assignment hint higgsfield.ai/cli is the CLI landing page for this product. Several third-party 'Higgsfield' MCP servers exist, but none are vendor-published.

auth.token_refresh: CLI tokens are short-lived; on 'Session expired' the user runs login again. API keys are static and should be rotated if exposed.
auth.scopes_notes: REST API: a key ID plus secret pair sent as 'Authorization: Key KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET'; docs say Bearer tokens are not used. CLI uses 'higgsfield auth login', a browser sign-in with short-lived tokens. No OAuth2 flow found in the sources read.

access.production_restrictions: No subscription is needed, but each API request is paid from a prepaid USD balance (minimum top-up $5) and a payment method must be registered. Invoice billing exists for committed-use contracts. Rate limits depend on account and model. Sources conflict on whether the CLI needs a paid higgsfield.ai subscription (one third-party guide says so; unverified).

resources: Image and video generation requests (model-specific schemas)
api.rate_limits: Depend on account and selected model (no numbers published in sources read).
api.limitations: Public API surface appears to be generation-focused: submit generation requests, read request status, cancel queued requests. No broad CRUD over account resources was found. Exact rate limits not published in pages read.

open_questions: Exact rate limits per model/account are not published in the pages read.
Whether a sandbox or free trial credit exists for API testing is unknown.
Whether the CLI and MCP require a paid higgsfield.ai subscription conflicts between sources (one third-party guide says yes).
The hosted MCP endpoint (mcp.higgsfield.ai) was not directly verified; a community README says it uses OAuth, which is unconfirmed.
No official MCP server repository was found on the higgsfield-ai GitHub org; the official MCP appears to be hosted, not open source.
A third-party Apidog post claims Bearer auth, which conflicts with the official docs; treated as unreliable.
Full endpoint list and the OpenAPI spec were not retrieved; the overview page gave no paths.
